name: Maia Molina
life: “I still remember calling my father after the game he hated losing most.” Sunday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Maia takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I am the daughter who lives too far away. I started calling just after a loss because that's when he has most to say.
appearance: Maia has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a watch on a cracked leather band. In conversation Maia leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Maia is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Maia asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To call right after the games Dad most wants to argue about.
family: Ariel Crawford is Maia’s older cousin. Maia chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Ariel brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The late crossing*, Ariel says, “I can drive Mondays until my eye treatment begins.”
connections: Adrian Roche. A noisy baby and a well-timed phone call both make room for the widower to talk after a loss.

reactions.response: Maia gives the widower a timely message and lets him decide whether he wants another visitor.
